text: Ethernet has a CRC, IP has a header checksum, TCP has a checksum, TLS has a MAC. What does this illustrate?
choices: Duplicated function — a genuine cost of layering, which IPv6 addressed by removing the IP header checksum entirely
explanation: Four integrity mechanisms on the same bytes, because each layer was designed not to trust the others. The IPv6 designers concluded the IP header checksum was waste, since Layer 2 and Layer 4 both check anyway — a rare instance of a standards body removing something.
